language.script_notes: Latin alphabet with the distinctive letters ı (dotless i), İ (dotted capital), ş, ğ, ç, ö and ü. Kurdish appears on some signs in the southeast, and Syriac on a few in Mardin.

road_furniture.bollard_color: Plain white rectangular bollards with a red reflector on the front, slightly fatter than the Australian or Dutch types; a rare yellow version appears in high-snowfall areas.
road_furniture.bollard_shape: Thin in profile from the side, rectangular from the front.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Standard steel guardrail on main roads.
road_furniture.line_paint: White edge lines and center lines; yellow used at some works zones.
road_furniture.curb_style: Painted black-and-white or red-and-white kerbs in towns; wide roads with undulating terrain even in urban areas.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Distinctive red-and-white arrows mark corners. Directional signs are either blue or green. Kilometre markers show a number (sometimes a letter) in the top-left corner giving the road number. Many utility poles are metal with large holes, larger than the holes on Romanian, Hungarian or Polish poles. Ankara alone has street signs with a curved top-middle section.

architecture.roof_style: Flat concrete roofs with rooftop water tanks and solar water heaters on apartment blocks; red-tiled pitched roofs on houses in the west and south.
architecture.roof_material: Red clay tile on pitched roofs; flat concrete and corrugated metal elsewhere.
architecture.wall_construction: Concrete-frame apartment blocks of five or more storeys fill towns and cities; stone houses in the east and southeast; timber and stone traditional houses in some historic towns. Mosques with slim pencil-shaped minarets and a central dome stand in every settlement.
architecture.wall_color_palette: White, cream and pastel apartment blocks with satellite dishes and balcony enclosures; honey-coloured or dark basalt stone in the southeast.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Mosques with one or more slender minarets in every town; concrete apartment blocks; Ottoman-era stone bridges, hamams and caravanserais; Atatürk statues and Turkish flags in squares.

nature.vegetation: Olive groves, vineyards and pines along the Aegean and Mediterranean coasts; dry steppe on the central plateau; verdant forest, tea and hazelnut plantations along the wet Black Sea coast; sparse mountain steppe in the east.
nature.terrain: A large peninsula of great variety — coastal plains ringed by mountains, a high central plateau (Anatolia), rugged and snow-bound eastern mountains including Mount Ararat, and the Mesopotamian plain in the southeast.
nature.climate_signature: Mediterranean along the coasts, dry continental on the plateau, wet and green on the Black Sea coast, and harsh with long snowy winters in the east.

vehicles.plate_color: White plate with black text and a blue strip on the left carrying 'TR'.
vehicles.plate_format: A two-digit province code, then up to three letters and up to four digits (e.g. '34 ABC 123', where 34 is Istanbul and 06 is Ankara).
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Many Fiats, Renaults and Fords are built locally; yellow taxis and dolmuş minibuses; tractors and small trucks on rural roads.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Dense across the west and centre and along main highways; coverage in the far east and southeast is thinner and older.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Neighbouring Mediterranean and Balkan landscapes and similar concrete-block towns
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Latin letters such as ı, İ, ş and ğ, TR plates with a province number, plain white red-reflector bollards and mosques with pencil minarets differ from Greek and Bulgarian scripts, plates and churches.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Caucasus mountains and green Black Sea coastal landscape near the northeast border
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Georgian and Azerbaijani scripts and plates differ; the Turkish province-number plate and red-and-white corner arrows are found here.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared eastern mountains and steppe near the border
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Persian script and Iranian plates versus Latin-script Turkish signs and the TR plate with province number.
